content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Describe the main types of microscopes and their uses
Explain the difference between magnification and resolution
Use a light microscope to observe cells
Most cells are too small to see with the naked eye.
is the use of microscopes to view objects that cannot be seen with the unaided eye. The development of microscopes has been crucial for understanding cell biology.
Robert Hooke first observed cells in 1665 using an early microscope. Since then, microscope technology has advanced dramatically, allowing us to see increasingly fine details of cell structure.
is how much larger an image appears compared to the actual object.
is the ability to distinguish between two separate points that are close together. It's about the clarity and detail of the image.
High magnification with low resolution = large, blurry image
The best microscope has both high magnification AND high resolution

content.text: To observe plant cells (e.g., onion epidermis) using a light microscope
Peel a thin layer of epidermis from an onion
Place on a slide with a drop of iodine solution
Observe under low power first, then higher powers
Draw and label what you observe
Cell wall visible around each cell
Higher magnification always means better images
Resolution is just as important. Without good resolution, higher magnification just makes a blurry image bigger
Electron microscopes produce black and white images. Colour is added artificially (false colour) to highlight structures
You can see individual atoms with any microscope
Even electron microscopes cannot easily resolve individual atoms in biological specimens
